diagnosis.highest_confidence_root_cause: THE DESIGN SURFACE IS ALMOST EMPTY AND ONE OF ITS EIGHT ROWS IS A WATER MAIN. The elevation read assigned a height to 17 contours: 9 existing (6,122 ft of the 51,605 ft of drawn existing contour linework, 11.9%) and 8 proposed (6,981 ft of 37,458 ft, 18.6%). Seven of the eight proposed rows are C-TOPO index contours at a 5 ft interval; the eighth, chain 6152 at z 7720, is the 10 in water main (style 168 SE-P-UT-WATER-10'', 1,756 ft - a quarter of the proposed surface's length) picked up by the radius label read. The 88-chain PROPOSED CONTOUR family (25,028 ft) and the 73-chain PROPOSED 1-FT CONTOURS family (11,337 ft) carry NO elevation. A TIN over eight far-apart index contours plus a pipe interpolates a 4-12 ft fill blanket across the ring: 43,800 of the 47,028 CY of fill sits in cells 4 ft or deeper (over about 150,000 SF), and 28,543 CY (61%) lies more than 25 ft from any proposed contour that has an elevation.
diagnosis.second: THE AREA. Our ring (312,044 SF) is 39% larger than his Clear & Grub (224,058 SF) and 2.2x his C3.0 limits markup (142,760.6 SF). The ring is open by 247.8 ft and bridged in 7 places (largest 153 ft); the bridging may enclose ground the drawn limit does not. Strip and fence follow the area.
diagnosis.third: THE STRIP TERM. Lowering the existing surface 0.67 ft adds 6,037 CY of fill and takes 1,338 CY of cut (47,028 vs 40,991 fill; 8,793 vs 10,131 cut). His Site Fill carries the topsoil respread on its own lines (Rough Place Topsoil 2,865 CY), so an apples-to-apples fill against his line is closer to our no-strip figure.
